summary: Slow eviction of prefetch requests in continuous batcher causing interleaved p99 latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using Dedicated pools (Acme Retail) are reporting intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes and request timeouts for short streaming workloads. Spikes coincide with bursts of small requests and appear as interleaved long-tail batches in traces. Impact: Several API calls for storefront personalization hit p99 > 2s and occasional 504s during a 20-40 minute window.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency p99 increased from ~320ms to 1.8-2.4s during incidents.
- ~12 failed requests (504) observed for Acme Retail in the affected window.
- Affects dedicated pool in us-east serving redwood-compat-13b for personalization route.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated (reserved capacity) pool: dc-east-09
- Route: /v1/generate (streaming enabled) pinned to redwood-compat-13b:v3
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, Runtime: serving-runtime 3.6.1

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Traffic pattern: high fan-out of short streaming requests (avg tokens 30) from many connections.
2) Continuous-batcher receives interleaved normal requests and prefetch candidates (prefetch requests are produced by model prefetching feature).
3) Batcher holds onto prefetch messages longer than expected; when normal requests arrive they are merged into older prefetch windows producing mixed-age batches which delay flush.
4) Resulting mixed batches occasionally exceed p99 latency SLO and cause streaming disconnect/timeouts for short streams.

Observed metrics & traces:
- p95 stable; p99 shows intermittent spikes to 2s+ aligned with batch flush timestamps.
- Batch metadata in logs shows "batch_age_ms" values of 350-700ms, and some prefetch messages with "created_at" significantly older than batch flush time.
- Traces: span ids 8a7b2c... (example), linked at: https://tracing.redwood.internal/trace/8a7b2c
- Logs sample (serving-runtime): "coalesce: kept_prefetch=12 evicted_prefetch=1 flush_delay_ms=420"

Attachments:
- Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/p99/batcher-p99
- Sample trace: https://tracing.redwood.internal/trace/8a7b2c

Initial investigation notes:
- Issue started after rollout of PR 2142 (scheduler tweak for prefetch priority) on 2026-02-28.
- Correlation window between 2026-02-28 03:10 and 2026-02-28 04:05 shows p99 spikes across multiple dedicated pools under similar workload.
- Heap/CPU metrics show no obvious GC pause on the affected nodes during spike windows.
- Reproduced locally with synthetic traffic: enabling prefetch + high fanout of short streams reproduces mixed-age batches and p99 tail.

Hypothesis:
- The scheduler change lowered eviction pressure on prefetch entries, allowing prefetch messages to persist and be merged with newer ephemeral requests. When many small streams arrive, these stale prefetch entries create head-of-line mixing and delay flushes to keep batch coherence, increasing p99.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Rollback note: Rolled back PR 2142 on dc-east-09 at 2026-03-01 14:45 UTC for the affected pool.
- Temporary config: reduced continuous-batcher.prefetch_ttl_ms from 1000 -> 120 and reduced linger_ms for short-stream tenant to 20ms.
- Result: immediate p99 improvement observed in Acme Retail pool dropping from 1.9s -> 360ms within two minutes.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering to produce a hotfix that enforces age-based eviction for prefetch entries and a hard cap on prefetch queue length. (Assigned to Liam O'Connor)
- Add telemetry for "prefetch_age_percentiles" per-tenant and per-route.
- Add an integration test that simulates prefetch + short-stream fanout and asserts p99 < 400ms under load.
- Postmortem and runbook update to include safe default TTLs for prefetch entries.

investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-02-28 02:45 UTC: PR 2142 deployed to canary cluster.
- 2026-02-28 03:07 UTC: Acme Retail reports first p99 spike after traffic pattern changed.
- 2026-03-01 14:30 UTC: SRE confirms correlation with PR 2142.
- 2026-03-01 14:45 UTC: Rollback applied to dc-east-09 and temporary TTL/linger adjustments made.
Evidence gathered:
- Batch logs show "kept_prefetch" counts rising during spike windows.
- Local repro harness replicates behavior when prefetch eviction disabled.
- No underlying infra CPU/mem pressure found.
Open questions:
- Is there any tenant-facing configuration that modifies prefetch behavior and caused this customer to be more impacted?
- Does prefetch eviction interact poorly with tenant reweighting?
resolution:
Workaround: Rolled back scheduler change (PR 2142) on affected Dedicated pools and applied conservative prefetch_ttl_ms and reduced linger for short-stream tenants. Permanent fix: engineering to merge hotfix branch hotfix/evict-prefetch-age which enforces age-based eviction and a max-prefetch-queue-size. Post-deploy verification plan: canary on single dedicated pool + 1h of synthetic short-stream fanout test + 24h monitoring window for p99 and evicted_prefetch metrics.

Follow-ups assigned:
- Liam O'Connor: deliver hotfix and telemetry (ETA 2026-03-05).
- Priya Menon: update continuous-batcher runbook with emergency TTL rollback steps.
- Product: communicate timeline to Acme Retail and schedule maintenance window if broad rollout needed.

Status: In Progress (hotfix under review).
